articles.title: China Approves DeepSeek and MiniMax AI Models for Global Use Amid Proposed Export Controls - Tekedia
articles.summary: China Approves DeepSeek and MiniMax AI Models for Global Use Amid Proposed Export Controls  Tekedia
articles.full_text:
China has approved AI developers DeepSeek and MiniMax to make their artificial intelligence models available globally, according to a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster CCTV, highlighting Beijing’s effort to expand the international reach of its AI industry while tightening oversight of technologies considered sensitive to national security.
A post published on Thursday by the account said the two companies had received state approval for global use of their models. In a separate post on Friday, the account, Yuyuan Tantian, said overseas internet users had called on other Chinese developers of open-source large language models to follow suit.
The reported approvals come as China moves to establish clearer controls over the overseas deployment of advanced AI technology. On October 16, Beijing proposed export controls covering 23 AI technologies, including technologies related to AI models, agents and computing clusters.

The measures signal that China intends to balance the international expansion of its AI industry with restrictions on transferring capabilities it considers strategically sensitive. For Chinese developers seeking overseas customers, regulatory approval could become an important factor in determining where and how their models can be deployed.
China’s commerce ministry said when the proposed controls were announced that most AI technologies would remain eligible for export. The ministry also indicated that licensing procedures would be simplified for exports of open-source technologies and for Chinese companies operating their own computing centers overseas.
The proposed restrictions nevertheless cover the overseas deployment of AI models that contain restricted technology. This creates a distinction between the broad availability of Chinese AI products and the transfer or use of capabilities that Beijing wants to keep under closer supervision.
This distinction is essential given the several forms international AI deployment can take. Developers may release model weights for external use, provide access through online services, license technology to foreign businesses or operate computing infrastructure outside China. The regulatory treatment of these arrangements may differ depending on the technology involved and the applicable export requirements.
For developers, greater clarity over which models and deployment arrangements are approved could reduce uncertainty when pursuing overseas business. However, the reported approvals for DeepSeek and MiniMax do not, by themselves, establish that every model, service or technology offered by either company is exempt from the proposed controls.
The status of the measures is also important. The source describes the October 16 announcement as a proposal, rather than a fully implemented export-control regime. The precise scope of the rules, their licensing requirements, and how they will be applied could therefore determine the practical effect on Chinese AI companies.
Beijing’s approach comes amid intensifying technological competition with Washington. Both countries are seeking to develop advanced AI capabilities while limiting access to technologies they regard as important to economic and national security. China’s proposed controls are its latest effort to regulate the transfer of AI tools and infrastructure that officials consider sensitive.
Global Expansion Offers Opportunities for Chinese AI Developers
The reported approvals could support efforts by DeepSeek and MiniMax to broaden their international presence, particularly among developers and businesses interested in open-source AI models.
Open-source and open-weight systems can allow customers to run models on their own infrastructure, adapt them for specific applications, and reduce dependence on a single commercial provider. For businesses, that flexibility can be attractive where data control, deployment costs and customization are important considerations.
International adoption can also help AI developers build larger user communities, attract commercial partners and identify new revenue opportunities. But approval to deploy models globally does not guarantee that foreign customers will adopt them at scale. Developers must still compete on performance, cost, reliability, technical support, and the availability of computing infrastructure.
The invitation for other Chinese open-source model developers to follow DeepSeek and MiniMax also points to the possibility of a broader industry-wide effort to secure permission for overseas deployment. If other companies obtain similar approvals, Chinese AI models could gain wider access to international markets, although the extent of that expansion will depend on the final regulatory framework and individual companies’ commercial strategies.

articles.title: Southern industries experienced positive growth, with exports reaching $138.4 billion. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Southern industries experienced positive growth, with exports reaching $138.4 billion.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
In the first nine months of the year, industrial production in many southern localities increased at a rate higher than the national average; total retail sales of goods and service revenue reached nearly 2.86 trillion VND.
Industry and trade in the south maintain growth momentum.
On the morning of October 22nd, the 12th Conference of Industry and Trade Sectors of Southern Provinces and Cities in 2026, themed "Strengthening regional cooperation and linkages to unlock resources and contribute to double-digit economic growth in the 2026-2030 period," was held in Ho Chi Minh City. The conference was organized by the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City in coordination with the Ministry of Industry and Trade (Industry Department, Planning and Finance Department) and the Departments of Industry and Trade of southern provinces and cities.
Speaking at the conference, Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Phan Thi Thang acknowledged the achievements of the industry and trade sectors in the localities over the past nine months, despite numerous difficulties. Specifically, the industrial production index (IIP) in the southern region increased by 12.9%, higher than the national average of 12.3%. Total retail sales of goods and services reached approximately 2.86 trillion VND, an increase of 16.5%, higher than the national average of 13.4% and accounting for 48.2% of the national market size. Export turnover reached 138.4 billion USD, an increase of 10.9%, accounting for 31.9% of the national export turnover.
In particular, industrial, commercial, and energy infrastructure continues to receive investment attention. Many localities have connected agricultural product consumption and OCOP (One Commune One Product) products, supported businesses in accessing free trade agreements, and applied e-commerce. Notably, initiatives such as the data-driven market management model in Tay Ninh ; connecting supply sources and distribution systems in Ho Chi Minh City; and innovating trade promotion and sales methods in the digital environment in the Mekong Delta provinces have been successful.
You may also like
The conference acknowledged that southern localities have leveraged their strengths in processing and manufacturing industries, high technology, logistics, agricultural and aquatic product exports, renewable energy, and border trade . Activities connecting supply and demand, promoting trade, focused promotions, and the application of digital technology have contributed to maintaining growth in industry, trade, services, and import-export.
In 2025, the industrial production index (IIP) of 5 out of 8 provinces and cities in the region increased higher than the national average of 9.2%. This growth momentum continued in the first nine months of this year, with 6 out of 8 provinces and cities having IIPs higher than the national average of 12.3%. Tay Ninh led with a 15% increase, followed by Vinh Long with 14.4%, An Giang with 13.7%, Dong Thap with 13%, Ca Mau with 12.7%, and Dong Nai City with 12.6% compared to the same period last year.
In particular, trade activities continued to be a bright spot in the southern region. In the first nine months, total retail sales of goods and services reached VND 2,858,823 billion, an increase of 16.5% compared to the same period last year, accounting for 48.2% of the total retail sales of goods and services nationwide. Ho Chi Minh City contributed the most, accounting for 52.1% of the region's total trade and service revenue. Following closely behind were Dong Nai, An Giang, Can Tho, Tay Ninh, Vinh Long, Dong Thap, and Ca Mau . Notably, all localities in the region recorded higher growth rates than the national average.
Regarding exports, the total value of goods from the southern region in the first nine months of 2026 is estimated at US$138.4 billion, an increase of 10.9% compared to the same period, accounting for 31.9% of the country's total export value. Businesses continue to take advantage of tariff preferences from free trade agreements to enhance competitiveness and expand markets.
Removing bottlenecks and accelerating progress in the final months of the year.
However, alongside the achievements, the Conference also pointed out bottlenecks that need to be addressed. The region's export growth reached 10.9%, lower than the national average of 24.5%; the progress of power generation projects, industrial park and cluster infrastructure, and logistics infrastructure has not met expectations. The rate of localization and deep processing remains limited; and the situation of trade fraud, counterfeit goods, and goods of unknown origin in the digital environment remains complex.
You may also like
PHOTO: CONTRIBUTOR
Deputy Minister Phan Thi Thang requested that units under the Ministry of Industry and Trade and the Departments of Industry and Trade focus on seven key tasks in the last quarter of the year. Specifically, these include: reviewing targets, developing operational scenarios for the fourth quarter and the 2027 plan; resolving obstacles and accelerating the progress of industrial, infrastructure, and energy investment projects; ensuring energy security, operating the power system safely, and maintaining the supply of petroleum products; developing the domestic market, stockpiling essential goods, stabilizing the market during the Tet holiday, and strengthening market management; promoting exports, leveraging FTAs, expanding markets, and improving product quality; continuing administrative reforms, removing difficulties for businesses, and improving coordination between the Ministry and localities; strengthening discipline and order in the performance of official duties, enhancing the responsibility of leaders, and proactively handling emerging issues.
Mr. Nguyen Loc Ha, Permanent Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee, stated that in the context of an economy requiring rapid, sustainable development and enhanced competitiveness, regional linkages in the South are of strategic importance. The last three months of the year are crucial for achieving the year's growth targets and preparing the conditions for implementing economic development tasks for the 2026-2030 period. Accordingly, Ho Chi Minh City will intensify trade promotion programs, supply and demand connections, concentrated promotions, trade fairs and exhibitions, year-end shopping activities, and trade and tourism events. Simultaneously, it will strengthen coordination with other provinces and cities in promoting and introducing products, connecting businesses, and expanding distribution systems.

articles.title: Geopolitical shocks are reconfiguring the Swiss industry’s coffee supply chains - SWI swissinfo.ch
articles.summary: Geopolitical shocks are reconfiguring the Swiss industry’s coffee supply chains  SWI swissinfo.ch
articles.full_text:
War is a top concern for Swiss coffee traders and alternative routes a top priority. But adapting supply chains in an era of constant disruption is no easy task.
Next time you sip a cup of coffee you can thank the Swiss Coffee Trade Association (SCTA). SCTA members – such as Nestlé, Starbucks, Sucafina, Olam, COFCO and LDC – represent over half of the coffee volume traded globally. Switzerland is a globally important coffee trading hub but threats to shipping routes and rising oil prices are pressuring supply chains. Participants polled at this year’s SCTA annual forum on October 1 listed “war” as their main cause for concern and “flexibility and alternative routes” as their top priority.
Shipping woes
Coffee beans are grown and harvested in South America, Asia and Africa. The beans called “green coffee” must then be transported across oceans to Europe and North America where most coffee roasters are based. According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), of the 183.6 million 60kg bags of coffee harvested in 2025, 77% was exported via 246 different routes. The most popular routes by volume are exports out of Brazil, Colombia and Vietnam to Europe or the United States. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz since February has not had a major impact on coffee trade but has forced carriers to reroute vessels and add fuel surcharges which have had a knock-on effect on coffee traders. The shortest shipping route between Asia and Europe have effectively been closed. Shipments of coffee beans from Vietnam must take the longer route via the Cape of Good Hope.
“We operate as a network. If one route is affected it has a knock-on effect on our entire shipping fleet,” a senior executive at a European shipping company told coffee traders at the SCTA forum. The executive wished to remain anonymous because the comments were made as part of a panel discussion meant for coffee traders.
According to the executive, rerouting coffee through the Cape of Good Hope increased transit time for their shipments by 20 days from Asia to Europe.
The new norm
It remains to be seen if such route diversions become the norm. Maritime research firm Drewery estimates that Suez Canal transits will return to 80% of their pre-diversion levels by February 2027. However, cost savings from shorter shipping time compared to the Cape of Good Hope will not be as significant as before because from now on insurers are likely to charge a war-risk premium which the shipping companies will pass on to coffee traders as surcharges.
“Coffee traders must get used to fast and bold decision-making with incomplete information because this ‘never normal’ situation will continue and exception management will be critical,” the shipping company executive said.
More
How Switzerland became a land of coffee
The Hormuz crisis thus served as a kind of litmus test for the resilience of coffee traders’ supply chains.
“Companies doing well now are the ones that were well-prepared. The companies that waited longer to adapt to longer shipping times did not do so well,” says Dany Barkha, global head of logistics at Geneva-based coffee trader Sucafina.
The company chose to act fast and commit to the longer transit time rather than wait to see how the situation would evolve.
“Putting the coffee on water with delayed transit time is better than waiting for the unknown. And the unknown is still not known till date after months of conflict,” says Barkha.
According to Barkha, resilience will not be an option but a compulsory core skill in supply chain management. He says in the future, coffee traders should invest in diversification of routes, smart inventory planning and strengthening relationships with shipping companies. Sucafina invested in a combination of all three to ensure a resilient supply chain.
“Diversification of routes gave us flexibility. Smart inventory planning bought us time and the carrier relationship gave us solutions when we hit severe disruptions,” says Barkha.
Rethinking supply chain planning
“In most cases, coffee supply chain is ‘just-in-time’. Roasters know they can buy spot coffee and survive a couple of weeks during a crisis,” says José Luis Pérez, head of commodities at Commodity Supplies AG. The canton Schwyz-based ocean freight broker has around 200 coffee customers.
According to Pérez, this “just-in-time” strategy is no longer as attractive as before because unexpected conflicts and changing government policies occur more often. The more time the coffee shipment is at sea, the more money a roaster loses as they have to make up for any shortfall by sourcing beans from warehouses more expensively. To avoid running out of beans, coffee roasters are now obliged to have larger inventories even if it means tying up more working capital and increases in financing and insurance costs.
“Five to 10 years ago the focus was on efficient supply chains, now it is resilient supply chains and in the future it will be adaptable supply chains,” Pérez concludes.
More
Better latte than never: Swiss coffee industry joins forces to improve conditions of coffee growers
Being adaptable means letting go of the old ways that no longer serve their purpose. Some of the supply chain planning in the coffee industry is no longer fit for purpose after the Hormuz crisis, according to Aleks Sidorecs, global head of supply chain at Swiss coffee trading firm Volcafe.
Instead of focusing on reports from the last month, he says the industry will have to keep track of leading shipping indicators that signal where disruptions are likely to happen, such as pre-shipment sample approval status, shipping instructions status and booking placed and accepted.
“These indicators give coffee industry players advance signals of potential disruptions and help them plan accordingly,” says Sidorecs.
The price of a cup of coffee
Reduced supply and increased demand have pushed green coffee prices to record highs over the last two years. ICO reported the first surplus in five years for 2025/2026 but consumers are still paying more because beans bought expensively are still circulating in supply chains. For example, price increases accounted for 4.7% of Nestlé’s coffee sales growth in the first half of the year. The Swiss multinational with brands like Nespresso and Nescafe expects lower green coffee prices in the second half of the year but cautioned investors that this will be “offset by some higher transportation and energy costs arising from the Middle East conflict”.
Weather conditions in top coffee producing countries like Brazil or Vietnam play a much bigger role in determining coffee prices than logistics costs. However, shipping bottlenecks can compound existing price pressure, especially when supply is already tight. Burkha reiterates that the cost of coffee isn’t only shaped at its origin and when logistics becomes more expensive, coffee becomes more expensive to move, store, and deliver.
“Not every increase reaches the consumer directly, but the pressure builds across the value chain. And that is why efficient logistics matters more than ever,” he says.

articles.title: Japanese FDI supports green transition in Vietnam’s manufacturing sector - Vietnam+ (VietnamPlus)
articles.summary: Japanese FDI supports green transition in Vietnam’s manufacturing sector  Vietnam+ (VietnamPlus)
articles.full_text:
Ho Chi Minh City (VNA) – Japanese Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is strengthening Vietnam’s manufacturing capacity and accelerating the green transition, as more Japanese companies expand production and adopt sustainable industrial solutions. 
Vietnam has become an important market and strategic manufacturing base in Southeast Asia for Japanese investors, reflecting their long-term confidence in the country’s economic potential and sustainable growth prospects. 
Investment cooperation has been a key pillar of Vietnam-Japan economic ties. According to the Vietnam Trade Promotion Agency under the Ministry of Industry and Trade, Japan has more than 5,800 active investment projects in Vietnam, with total registered capital exceeding 81 billion USD. 
Free trade agreements (FTAs) have also created favourable conditions for businesses in both countries through tariff reductions, rules of origin, and trade facilitation, opening up opportunities for deeper participation in regional production networks and supply chains. 
Major Japanese companies, including Honda, Panasonic, Kao Vietnam and Sumitomo, have maintained and expanded their operations in Vietnam. Meanwhile, new Japanese investment is flowing into industrial parks, supporting greener manufacturing and the adoption of more sustainable production solutions. 
A recent example is Japanese group Oji’s launch of construction of a new aseptic carton packaging factory under its Oji Liquid Pak (OLP) brand. The project, with an investment of 110 million USD, is located in Long Thanh High-Tech Park in Dong Nai province. 
The investment demonstrates Oji Liquid Pak’s long-term commitment to Vietnam and reinforces the country’s role as a strategic manufacturing and supply hub for the group in Southeast Asia. It is also expected to support the region’s shift towards circular packaging solutions that meet evolving policy requirements. 
Nguyen Quoc An, deputy head of the Dong Nai Industrial and Economic Zones Authority (DNIEZA), said large-scale projects like this would contribute to local industrial development, strengthen domestic production capacity and help Vietnamese businesses participate more deeply in regional supply chains. 
The authority pledged to support investors throughout project implementation, provide timely guidance and coordinate efforts to resolve difficulties so that projects can proceed in line with regulations and begin operations as soon as possible. 
Oji Liquid Pak General Director Kestutis Sliuzas said manufacturing industries, including packaging, were moving towards new standards that combine state-of-the-art recyclable materials and packaging, efficiency, and food safety. 
The new factory will combine food packaging production with research and development, technical services, and the installation and maintenance of Japanese machinery and equipment. These activities are expected to contribute to a modern industrial environment with higher quality and added value. 
Japanese investment also covers research and development in natural sciences, machinery repair and maintenance, equipment installation, and the import, export, and distribution of goods in accordance with Vietnamese law. 
Tran Viet Ha, Deputy Head of the Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing and Industrial Zones Authority (HEPZA), said the authority was working to help investors start projects sooner after registration and reduce procedures related to planning and construction. 
HEPZA aims to resolve matters within its authority directly and coordinate with other agencies on issues requiring inter-agency cooperation. It is also shifting from a focus on administrative procedures to monitoring projects throughout their life cycle, from investment preparation to operation. 
These efforts align with Politburo Resolution No. 10-NQ/TW, dated June 8, 2026, on developing the foreign-invested economy. The resolution shifts Vietnam’s investment attraction strategy towards quality rather than quantity, prioritising high technology, innovation, workforce development and technology transfer. 
The policy direction reflects Vietnam’s ambition to move beyond labour-intensive assembly towards becoming a technology-driven investment destination that generates higher added value and supports sustainable industrial growth./.

articles.title: Temu & IACC launch direct anti-counterfeit channel - Australia
articles.summary: Temu & IACC launch direct anti-counterfeit channel  Australia
articles.full_text:
Temu and the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition have expanded their collaboration with a dedicated intellectual property protection programme. The initiative gives IACC member brands a direct route to escalate complex cases on Temu.
The IACC-Temu Program is a voluntary scheme that adds a separate support channel for member brands alongside Temu's existing reporting tools, which remain open to all rights holders. Under the arrangement, participating brands can raise pending or rejected notices, as well as cases requiring further review, through the IACC Global Portal.
Each escalation submitted through the programme will receive a response within 48 hours, Temu said. Brands in the scheme can also submit keywords and images to help the marketplace identify potentially infringing listings before complaints are filed.
The move builds on a relationship that also includes Temu's membership of the IACC as a General Member earlier this year. It gives brands access to direct support from Temu's intellectual property specialists, quarterly check-ins, detailed feedback and periodic status reports.
Bob Barchiesi, President of the IACC, said the programme followed earlier discussions between the organisation and the online marketplace.
"Temu underscored its commitment to brand protection and collaboration with the IACC when its Co-Founder, Dada Sun, met with me and my team. That discussion marked an important step in strengthening our relationship and ultimately led to the launch of the IACC-Temu Program," Barchiesi said.
"Early results from our joint program have been positive for our member brands, demonstrating the immense value of collaboration between all stakeholders in addressing IP challenges," he added.
How it works
The programme is designed for more difficult disputes rather than as a replacement for standard reporting systems. Rights holders that are not part of the IACC scheme can still use Temu's existing channels to report alleged infringements.
For brands that do join, the additional route is intended for notices that remain unresolved or need another review. The option to provide keywords and images also ties brand owners more closely to Temu's monitoring process, which scans listings for possible infringements before products are flagged through external complaints.
Temu's intellectual property controls cover seller vetting, pre-listing screening and round-the-clock post-listing monitoring, according to the company. Its 2026 Intellectual Property Protection Report says 331 potentially infringing listings were removed proactively for every complaint-based takedown.
The report also says Temu's proactive monitoring database now covers more than 15,000 brands, about three times the previous year's level. It uses more than 47 million images and 9.5 million keywords, with submissions from participating brands under the IACC-Temu Program feeding into the system.
Broader pressure
Online marketplaces have faced sustained scrutiny from brands, trade groups and regulators over counterfeit goods and other intellectual property disputes. In response, platforms have expanded notice-and-takedown systems, introduced automated screening tools and built direct relationships with rights holders to improve enforcement.
The tie-up between Temu and the IACC reflects a wider shift towards more structured cooperation between marketplaces and brand owners. For trade groups such as the IACC, direct escalation channels can give members a faster route through platform enforcement processes when standard submissions do not resolve a case.
For marketplaces, such arrangements can also provide more data on repeat patterns, suspect keywords and imagery linked to disputed goods. That can help identify listings earlier, although the effectiveness of such systems often depends on the quality of brand-supplied information and the speed of platform review.
A Temu spokesperson said the company sees enforcement and cooperation as linked parts of its intellectual property approach.
"Effective IP protection requires both strong enforcement measures and close collaboration with rights holders," the spokesperson said.
"The IACC-Temu Program brings these efforts together to better address complex cases and support proactive enforcement."

articles.title: Canada unveils $6.2bn plan to shield manufacturers as US tariffs bite - Euronews.com
articles.summary: Canada unveils $6.2bn plan to shield manufacturers as US tariffs bite  Euronews.com
articles.full_text:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said the Trump tariffs make both US and Canadian industries weaker and reduce choice for households in both countries.
Canada has announced a $6.2 billion (€5.7 billion) package to protect its steel and auto industries from US tariffs, as Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that Washington has permanently altered a trade relationship built over decades.
Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford jointly unveiled the plan on Wednesday, directing $3.7 billion (€3.4 billion) to steelmakers and $1.8 billion (€1.65 billion) to automakers over five years, with $1.1 billion (€1 billion) of the auto funding coming from the federal government in Ottawa.
The announcement came the same day US-owned Cleveland-Cliffs confirmed layoffs at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant, underlining the human cost of the trade dispute.
“US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that’s existed for decades,” Carney said. “They’ve raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage.”
The damage to the auto sector is already visible in the trade figures, as Canadian auto exports to the US have fallen more than 10 percent, while US exports to Canada have dropped more than 20 percent, a decline Carney said hurts both sides of the border.
“Tariffs make both our industries weaker and reduce choice for our families,” he stressed.
Carney confirmed he spoke at length with President Trump on Wednesday, covering trade, Iran and the Middle East.
He signalled no breakthrough but said Canada remains ready to negotiate. Talks collapsed in August after Trump imposed 50% tariffs on around $20 billion (€18.4 billion) in Canadian goods, prompting Canadian retaliation.
For his part, Ford was direct about what the dispute has done to bilateral ties. “No matter what happens in the midterms, no matter who sits in the White House, we’re not going back to the way things were,” he said.
US embassy accuses Canada of meddling in midterms
Carney has set a target of doubling Canadian exports to non-US markets within a decade, acknowledging that an integrated North American auto industry may no longer be Washington’s priority.
“Their approach has changed,” he said. “So must ours.”
Meanwhile, the day took a sharper diplomatic turn when the US Embassy issued a statement accusing Canadian politicians of seeking to influence next month’s American midterm elections.
The embassy named Industry Minister Mélanie Joly for discussing retaliatory tariffs targeting Republican states and Ford for running a US television ad featuring former President Ronald Reagan criticising tariffs, the ad that prompted Trump to walk away from trade talks in October 2025.
Both leaders rejected the allegations. So did independent analysts.
“The implicit assumption that Canada could significantly alter the outcome of the midterms is absurd,” said Daniel Béland, political science professor at McGill University.

articles.title: Mitsubishi Power's $490 million Chatham County expansion to create 220 jobs - WJCL
articles.summary: Mitsubishi Power's $490 million Chatham County expansion to create 220 jobs  WJCLMitsubishi Power to invest $490M, add 220 jobs in Chatham County  WTOCMitsubishi Power facility plans $490 million expansion in response to AI, data center demand  The Business JournalsMitsubishi announce half-a-billion dollar expansion in Chatham County  YahooMitsubishi Power's $490M Investment in Georgia to Support Rising Power Generation Demand  Manufacturing.net
articles.full_text:
Above video: Your Friday headlines
Mitsubishi Power Americas plans to invest $490 million to expand its manufacturing operation in Chatham County, adding more than 220 jobs and nearly doubling the facility’s footprint, Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp announced Friday.
The company will add 450,000 square feet to its Savannah Machinery Works facility at 1000 Pine Meadow Drive near Pooler. The plant, visible to drivers traveling along Interstate 16, manufactures and assembles gas turbines used to generate electricity for homes and businesses.
Mitsubishi Power said the expanded facility is expected to begin operating in early 2029.
“The expansion includes a 450,000-square-foot increase in our footprint here at the site, an additional 220 new jobs for the region and advancements in manufacturing technology and overall capacity,” said Brandon Bodie, vice president of Savannah Machinery Works.
New jobs across several fields
The company expects to hire workers for positions in manufacturing, engineering, quality control, maintenance, logistics, operations and heavy machinery.
Local leaders said they hope to fill the temporary construction jobs and permanent positions with people who already live in the region.
Hugh “Trip” Tollison, president and CEO of the Savannah Economic Development Authority, said the project’s economic impact will begin before the expansion opens.
“When you think about a half-billion dollars going into one construction project, think about the labor that’s going to be needed to build the building and the concrete that’s going to be poured,” Tollison said.
He called the expansion a major win for Chatham County and said it was a highly competitive project.
“This is the largest investment to date on behalf of Mitsubishi Power Americas and will create meaningful new job opportunities for our community,” Tollison said.
Meeting growing electricity demand
Mitsubishi Power said it is expanding to keep pace with rising demand for electricity and power-generation equipment.
The company provides equipment and services for the energy industry, including gas, steam and aero-derivative turbines, geothermal systems and environmental controls. It also develops artificial intelligence technology designed to support autonomous power plant operations.
Bill Newsom, president and CEO of Mitsubishi Power Americas, said the expansion will strengthen domestic manufacturing while giving employees access to more advanced technology.
“This expansion strengthens American manufacturing and gives our people the advanced capabilities they need as they continue to deliver for our customers,” Newsom said.
Bodie said the company is also focused on developing a skilled local workforce.
“We’re excited about building a really strong workforce here that’s skilled and can support manufacturing in this community,” he said.
Building on a longtime Georgia presence
Mitsubishi Power has operated in Chatham County since 2009, when it established the Savannah Machinery Works operation during the Great Recession.
The expansion follows meetings Kemp and other state officials held with Mitsubishi Power and its parent company, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, in Tokyo.
“We are excited that the Savannah Machinery Works is expanding to turn those possibilities into reality,” Kemp said in a statement.
Georgia Economic Development Commissioner Pat Wilson said the state’s ports, railroads, highways and airports helped make the area attractive for the project. He also credited Georgia’s longstanding relationship with Mitsubishi Power.
“As demand for Mitsubishi Power’s products grows, this expansion is a reminder that economic development is about more than winning a project,” Wilson said. “It is about showing up, building relationships and being a long-term partner.”
The Georgia Department of Economic Development coordinated the project with the Savannah Economic Development Authority, Georgia Power and Georgia Quick Start.
Additional details about the construction and hiring schedules were not immediately available.

articles.title: China's SAFE Proposes 11 New Cross-Border Investment and Financing Measures, Expanding Corporate Foreign Debt and Outbound Remittance Quotas - BigGo Finance
articles.summary: China's SAFE Proposes 11 New Cross-Border Investment and Financing Measures, Expanding Corporate Foreign Debt and Outbound Remittance Quotas  BigGo Finance
articles.full_text:
On October 23, China's State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) opened public consultation on its "Notice on Matters Concerning Further Optimizing Cross-Border Investment and Financing Facilitation Policies (Draft for Comment)," unveiling 11 facilitation measures in three major categories in one go, covering direct investment, cross-border financing and capital account registration management. It marks another systematic easing in the opening of China's capital account, following the September 2025 reform deepening foreign exchange management for cross-border investment and financing.
SAFE Administrator Zhu Hexin had previously signaled at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Financial Street Forum annual meeting that a package of policies to optimize capital account foreign exchange management would be introduced, to better meet companies' cross-border investment, financing and capital allocation needs and to serve both "bringing in" and "going global."
According to a report by Yicai, a SAFE official said the policies were formulated on the basis of field research in multiple locations and feedback collected from banks and companies on foreign direct investment, cross-border financing and foreign exchange registration. Many of the measures are problem-oriented and, once implemented, are expected to resolve the difficulties reported by most companies.
Direct Investment: Doubled Quotas Alongside Simplified Documentation
Under direct investment, the policy focuses on raising the amount of funds companies can use and reducing duplicative reviews. The cap on direct settlement and payment of capital account income (capital funds and foreign debt funds) rises from the current equivalent of $200,000 per institution per month to $500,000. Companies can directly settle foreign exchange and transfer funds into their onshore yuan accounts on the strength of a payment instruction letter, while still subject to the negative list on the use of capital account income. The previous rules on using capital account income under the guise of petty cash will no longer apply.
At the same time, a channel for remitting petty cash for outbound direct investment has been opened. Onshore institutions may, on the strength of a statement of intended use, remit funds of up to the equivalent of $200,000 per month — and no more than 10% of the institution's cumulative registered outbound direct investment remittance quota — to cover daily small expenses of overseas entities such as rent, utilities, personnel, office, transportation, taxes and miscellaneous purchases. Regulators made clear that those who fail to use petty cash for the stated purposes will be dealt with according to law, with facilitation and risk control designed in tandem.
For situations involving multiple foreign exchange payments for the same overseas purpose, if the transaction is handled again at the same bank branch, the bank may, based on how the first transaction was handled and its understanding of the client and the business, be exempt from re-reviewing supporting documents on the use of funds. In special cases — such as overseas investment projects requiring pre-investment capital verification or investment destinations requiring paid-in registered capital — companies may first process the remittance on the strength of a statement of the fund use plan and an undertaking to supply supplementary materials later, and must complete the materials within the undertaking period or before the next remittance, whichever comes first.
Cross-Border Financing: Broader Eligibility and Lower Risk Factors
The core of the debt-financing measures is to broaden the reach of high-level opening. The scope of entities eligible for cross-border financing facilitation is further expanded: technology companies including innovative small and medium-sized enterprises, manufacturing "single champion" enterprises, science and technology reform demonstration enterprises, (national) enterprise technology centers, enterprises in the smart factory tiered cultivation system (advanced level and above), and enterprises on the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs' list of key laboratories may borrow foreign debt within a quota of up to the equivalent of $10 million; eligible "innovation points system" enterprises have a cap of the equivalent of $20 million.
Under the macro-prudential management framework, the category risk conversion factor for eligible foreign-invested enterprises borrowing foreign debt from overseas related parties is cut from 1 to 0.5. The adjustment does not raise the macro-prudential cap on cross-border financing, but it reduces the extent to which related-party borrowing consumes a foreign-invested enterprise's own foreign debt quota — effectively freeing up more room within the existing pool.
The green foreign debt policy is also being extended from pilot programs to nationwide application: eligible companies borrowing foreign debt for green development or low-carbon transition projects will likewise see the category risk conversion factor cut from 1 to 0.5. Shared foreign debt quotas for financial leasing parent and subsidiary companies are also being rolled out nationwide: under the macro-prudential management model, subsidiaries of financial leasing companies whose own foreign debt quota is insufficient may use the unused quota of their parent companies to borrow foreign debt. The policy has been piloted in selected regions since 2018 and now covers the whole country.
Registration Management: Off-Site Handling and Online Processing to Cut Costs
The three measures on registration management target companies' time costs and the "legwork cost." The range of banks that can handle outbound direct investment registration is expanded from banks within the jurisdiction of the local SAFE office to banks in other cities within the territory of the provincial branch of the relevant SAFE office, allowing companies operating across regions to handle registration, amendment and cancellation nearby; the off-site handling bank must bear responsibility for authenticity and compliance review.
Under the macro-prudential management model, when eligible non-financial corporate debtors borrow offshore loans from the offshore departments of onshore banks, they may, at the time of drawdown or principal and interest repayment, handle non-fund-transfer registration at banks within the provincial branch's territory; such registration is shifted from processing by SAFE to direct processing by banks. In addition, administrative licensing matters under the capital account — including onshore institutions' overseas derivatives business, onshore guarantees for offshore loans, onshore institutions' offshore lending, and foreign claims formed by the performance of onshore guarantees for offshore loans — may be submitted online through the SAFE Digital Foreign Exchange Platform.
A comparison of the main policy adjustments follows:
| Policy Item | Current Arrangement | Draft for Comment | 
|---|---|---|
| Direct settlement and payment of capital account income | No more than the equivalent of $200,000 per month | No more than the equivalent of $500,000 per month | 
| Remittance of petty cash for outbound direct investment | No dedicated channel | No more than the equivalent of $200,000 per month, and no more than 10% of the registered remittance quota cumulatively | 
| Foreign debt facilitation quota for technology companies | High-tech enterprises, specialized and sophisticated SMEs, technology-based SMEs, etc. | Expanded to manufacturing single champions, science and technology reform demonstration enterprises, smart factories, etc. | 
| Risk factor for foreign-invested enterprises' related-party foreign debt | 1 | 0.5 | 
| Green foreign debt risk factor | Piloted in selected regions | Nationwide, with the factor cut from 1 to 0.5 | 
| Shared foreign debt quota for financial leasing parent and subsidiary companies | Piloted in selected regions | Nationwide | 
| Outbound direct investment registration | Banks within the jurisdiction of the local SAFE office | Off-site banks within the provincial branch's territory | 
Note: Current arrangements are compiled based on existing policy parameters disclosed by regulators.
Impact Analysis
From the corporate side, doubling the direct settlement and payment quota helps foreign-invested enterprises shorten the time funds sit in accounts and improves the efficiency of using foreign capital once it arrives; the petty cash remittance channel directly addresses the foreign exchange pain point of overseas institutions' daily operating expenses, and is particularly important for the overseas branches of companies going global. With the expanded eligibility for cross-border financing, more technology companies that occupy key positions in industrial chains but have limited net assets will gain foreign debt capacity far beyond net-asset constraints.
From the financial institution side, the push for off-site registration and online processing means banks will need to handle foreign exchange registration business across a wider geographic area, with compliance review responsibilities increasing accordingly; the shift of non-fund-transfer registration for offshore loans to direct bank processing also places higher demands on banks' business systems and internal controls.
From a macro perspective, this round of policies, without loosening the macro-prudential cap on cross-border financing, revitalizes existing quotas through risk factor adjustments and quota sharing, reflecting an approach of "no easing in aggregate, structural optimization." The nationwide rollout of green foreign debt ties foreign exchange management tools to green and low-carbon transition goals. The timing of implementation and final terms of the draft for comment remain subject to confirmation in a formal document from regulators.

articles.summary: Brent crude increase follows Tehran threatening retaliatory attacks on Gulf refineries and datacentresOil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets.Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April. Continue reading...
articles.full_text:
Oil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April.
The jump came after Tehran said it would attack oil facilities, undersea cables, datacentres and AI facilities in the Gulf region if a new US-Israeli offensive was launched against Iran.
Richard Hunter, of the broker Interactive Investor, said: “Widespread reports that the US is considering renewed military strikes on Iran after the midterm elections rather than pursuing a diplomatic route was enough for the price to pop, after what many had considered would be a brief conflict is now in its eighth month.”
The oil price later eased back slight to sit about 2.7% up at just over $116 a barrel. Brent crude had traded at about $72 a barrel back in February, before the Iran war began, but soared to touch $126 a barrel by the end of April.
Tensions in the region have been rising this week and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed to have struck four commercial ships in the strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The US state department ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which has faced continued attacks from Houthi rebels in Yemen.
Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at the broker Wealth Club, said fears were rising that American and Israeli forces would be ordered to launch strikes on Iran’s energy infrastructure after the US elections on 3 November.
She added: “At the same time, the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s facilities by Houthi rebels have intensified this week, and for ships attempting to cross the strait of Hormuz, it’s still a dangerous journey, with projectiles still being fired.”
Streeter said Ukraine’s bombardment of Russian diesel refineries was also adding to supply concerns.

AGENCY:
Agricultural Marketing Service, USDA.
ACTION:
Request for information.
SUMMARY:
The Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is seeking input from the public, including dairy industry stakeholders, on market conditions related to monthly route sales limits within the exempt plant definition in its regulations. AMS is requesting input on whether and how marketing conditions have changed since the definition was implemented in 1999.
DATES:
Comments must be received by November 23, 2026 to be considered.
ADDRESSES:
Interested persons are invited to submit comments concerning this notice. Comments may be submitted through the Federal e-rulemaking portal at
https://www.regulations.gov
and should reference the document number, date, and page number of this issue of the
Federal Register
. Written comments may be submitted via mail to USDA/AMS/Dairy Programs, Stop 0225—Room 2530, 1400 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20250-0225. All comments submitted in response to this notice, including the identity of the individuals or entities submitting the comments, will be included in the record and made available to the public, and can be viewed at
https://www.regulations.gov.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Erin Taylor, USDA/AMS/Dairy Programs, Order Formulation and Enforcement Division, STOP 0225—Room 2530, 1400 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20250-0225; telephone: (202) 720-4392; email address:
OFEB@usda.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
A nonpool plant is defined within the Federal milk marketing order (FMMO) regulations in 7 CFR 1000.8, which includes the definition for an exempt plant in § 1000.8(e), and specifically a definition for a
de minimis
plant exemption in § 1000.8(e)(4). The regulations were implemented in the Federal Milk Marketing Order Reform (Order Reform) final rule published on September 1, 1999 (64 FR 47898), and the definition of a nonpool plant has not been amended since.
To determine the monthly pounds threshold that would qualify a plant for an exemption under the
de minimis
definition being established during the Order Reform process, AMS reviewed the route sales limits of all FMMOs that had a
de minimis
exempt plant provision in place at the time. In an effort not to impose a pool obligation on any plant that was exempt for size at the time, AMS selected the highest plant exemption level allowed in any FMMO, which was 150,000 pounds or less of monthly route disposition.
In considering whether marketing conditions have changed since the definition was implemented in 1999, AMS seeks input from impacted dairy stakeholders on relevant market conditions, route disposition levels, and other related factors.
Request for Information
In this Request for Information (RFI), AMS will consider how fluid milk market conditions have changed since the
de minimis
route disposition limit in the exempt plant definition was implemented, as well as current fluid milk marketing conditions. Through this RFI, AMS is soliciting comments on the market effects for handlers currently operating an exempt plant, as well as the effects of the disposition limit on regulated handlers who are not exempt. All interested parties are encouraged to provide input during the comment period. AMS will review and consider all information submitted in response to this RFI.
Respondents may provide information for one or more of the questions or topics listed below, as desired.
1. What market conditions or other factors should AMS consider in evaluating the current
de minimis
exempt plant route disposition limit?
2. Has the dairy market changed in such a way that the 150,000 pound per month route disposition limit may no longer be appropriate? If so, how?
3. What plant data or other data should AMS consider in its evaluation of the
de minimis
exempt plant definition relative to the current marketing of fluid milk?
4. What impact on the industry—including on producers, handlers, and consumers—would a change in the
de minimis
exempt plant route disposition have, including any increasing or decreasing costs for producers, handlers, or consumers?
5. What effects does the
de minimis
exempt plant route disposition limit have on small businesses? Currently, the Small Business Administration defines a small fluid milk processing plant as a plant, or larger company operating multiple plants, with 1,150 or fewer employees collectively.

articles.title: India-US Trade Deal Talks, Russian Oil Imports And Ukraine Peace Formula - India Today - India Today
articles.summary: India-US Trade Deal Talks, Russian Oil Imports And Ukraine Peace Formula - India Today  India Today
articles.full_text:
On India First, Gaurav Sawant hosts strategic thinker Professor Brahma Chellaney, former diplomat Ambassador Yash Sinha, and India Today Group Editorial Director Raj Chengappa to evaluate the trajectory of India-US ties under the Trump administration. Chellaney warns of an institutional reset in Washington, noting that 'there is a calculated downgrading of India in US strategy' driven by a rethink after China's rise. Sinha highlights the purely transactional nature of the bilateral engagement, pointing to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to Jamnagar and Washington's push for India to process Venezuelan crude. Meanwhile, Chengappa shares insights from his interaction with Rubio regarding trade negotiations, tariff predictability, and global energy dynamics. The experts unpack the broader implications of US defence equipment supplies, military tech holdups, and how New Delhi must navigate strategic autonomy in an increasingly transactional global order.
India-US Trade Deal Talks, Russian Oil Imports And Ukraine Peace Formula
A detailed discussion examines critical dimensions of India-US bilateral ties following high-level interactions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Trump administration insider Sergio Gor. Addressing the status of trade negotiations, the conversation highlights India's key priorities, including securing a competitive advantage and achieving predictability against arbitrary tariff shifts under mechanisms like Section 301. The dialogue explores the rationale behind Washington's waiver on Russian fuel imports, where global economic stabilization and preventing worldwide fuel price inflation emerged as immediate imperatives. Furthermore, the discussion touches upon diplomatic efforts to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, specifically around Donbas. Analysis indicates that neither side can secure an outright military victory, emphasizing that lasting peace requires mutual concessions through dialogue and diplomacy.
LATEST VIDEOS
A video released following the firing attack on Tiger Shroff shows the extent of injuries sustained on the actor's arm, including gunpowder burns and wounds caused by shattered glass. Multiple rounds of bullets were fired at close range during the incident on Sunday night, leaving Shroff's driver and a fan injured and hospitalised. While the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack, Shroff's family confirmed the fan is receiving care, with the actor sharing the video with the caption 'God is kind.'
A massive controversy has erupted following the removal of protest photographs taken by Rehan Vadra from an exhibition at Delhi's Bikaner House. Panelists including art curator Kishore Singh, IIMUN founder Rishabh Shah, lawyer and Her Haq founder Anya Wick, Congress national spokesperson Gurmehar Kaur, and BJP national spokesperson Sanju Verma debated the issue of artistic freedom versus venue regulations. While arts advocates and the opposition argued that documenting public dissent through street photography should not face blanket censorship, Sanju Verma defended the venue's actions, asserting, 'Freedom of speech and freedom of expression under Article 19 of the Constitution are not absolute.' Verma stated that the exhibition violated specific Bikaner House guidelines restricting political content, rejecting allegations of political vendetta.
A preview of an upcoming interview on India Today outlines major developments in India-US relations, including discussions around a potential bilateral trade deal and an anticipated meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump. Key topics include strategic cooperation in nuclear energy through small modular reactor technology, joint military exercises involving F-35 aircraft, and India's position as a global refining superpower. The analysis highlights the operational capability of the Jamnagar refinery to process diverse crude grades such as Venezuelan and Russian Ural oil amid international energy supply disruptions. Strategic considerations also encompass potential Indian corporate investments in the United States and global energy security. Furthermore, the discussion touches on bilateral trade dynamics, addressing whether the India First and America First frameworks can align, concerns over tariff policies, and the imperative for supply chain diversification away from dependency on critical mineral imports from China.

articles.title: Vietnamese businesses have more opportunities to export to the Middle East and Africa. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Vietnamese businesses have more opportunities to export to the Middle East and Africa.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
(DTTC) - Along with tariff preferences from the CEPA Agreement, Vietnamese businesses have more opportunities to expand exports to the Middle East and Africa thanks to this agreement.
On October 23rd, in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ho Chi Minh City Trade and Investment Promotion Center (ITPC), in collaboration with the Import-Export Department ( Ministry of Industry and Trade ), organized a workshop titled "Vietnam-UAE CEPA Agreement: Export Potential to the Middle East and Africa for Vietnamese Businesses".
At the seminar, Mr. Pham Binh An, former Deputy Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Institute for Development Research, stated that the UAE's GDP is estimated to reach approximately $517.7 billion in 2025, with the non-oil economy accounting for 77%.
Mr. Pham Binh An, former Deputy Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Institute for Development Research, analyzes the potential of the UAE market. Photo: MINH XUAN
Due to natural conditions limiting agricultural production, the UAE has to import approximately 85%-90% of its food needs. Furthermore, foreigners make up 88.5% of the UAE population, creating a diverse consumer market and opening up significant opportunities for Vietnamese agricultural products, seafood, processed foods, and consumer goods.
The UAE also holds a central position as a trade transit hub between Asia, Europe, and Africa, with a well-developed port system, logistics infrastructure, and re-export operations that allow goods to quickly access many markets in the region. This is an advantage for Vietnamese businesses to leverage the UAE as a strategic distribution hub, rather than just a direct consumption market.
You may also like
Market access opportunities are further expanded now that the Vietnam-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) has come into effect on February 3, 2026.
Mr. Truong Xuan Trung, Head of the Vietnamese Trade Office in the UAE, further informed that the CEPA aims to eliminate tariffs on 99% of goods originating from Vietnam within the scope of the UAE's commitments, according to the applicable roadmap and conditions. Product groups with great potential for exploitation include: agricultural products, processed foods, seafood, textiles, footwear, wood products, furniture, and consumer goods.
However, tariff preferences do not necessarily mean easy market access for goods. Therefore, businesses should prioritize choosing the UAE as a location to test demand, improve product quality, and build strong relationships with importers.
Once a stable distribution network has been established, the business then expands to countries belonging to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), and subsequently selects Middle Eastern and African markets suitable for each product category.
Experts and businesses attended a workshop on the Vietnam-UAE CEPA Agreement, organized by ITPC in collaboration with the Import-Export Department on October 23rd in Ho Chi Minh City. Photo: MINH XUAN
You may also like
To maintain a sustainable supply chain, businesses need to carefully select capable partners, fully calculate transportation, warehousing, and distribution costs, and strictly adhere to food safety regulations, traceability, and Halal standards for mandatory product categories.
In particular, Vietnamese goods exported to the UAE and then re-exported to a third country do not automatically qualify for preferential tariffs under the CEPA.
Mr. Tran Ngoc Binh, Head of the Import-Export Management Department Region III, Import-Export Department, Ministry of Industry and Trade, said that the Ministry of Industry and Trade will focus on providing market information, training on Halal standards, supporting connections with importers, and creating conditions for businesses to participate in specialized exhibitions in the UAE, the Middle East, and Africa. This will help businesses improve their supply capacity, gradually build distribution networks, and expand their export market share.

articles.summary: India's exports to Germany could cross USD 50 billion by 2030: ASSOCHAM  www.malaysiasun.com
articles.full_text:
ANI
                
23 Oct 2026, 21:32 GMT+10
            
New Delhi [India], October 23 (ANI): India's exports of goods and services to Germany could exceed USD 50 billion by 2030, supported by greater use of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and deeper economic cooperation between the two countries, according to a report by the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India (ASSOCHAM).
The report was released by Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in Berlin.
The report highlighted the potential for expanding market access, investment and business partnerships between India and Germany. It said the two countries could use their respective strengths in manufacturing, technology and innovation to deepen economic ties and create new growth opportunities.
ASSOCHAM President Nirmal K. Minda said stronger industrial cooperation could help businesses in both countries, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The India-EU FTA is expected to provide fresh momentum to bilateral trade. According to ASSOCHAM, zero-duty access to a significant share of Indian exports to the European Union could benefit sectors such as textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, marine products, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals and electronics.
The report also identified opportunities in advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, digital technology, critical minerals and defence, where Germany's industrial capabilities could complement India's growing manufacturing and services sectors.
ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal said green growth was another promising area for cooperation.
He highlighted opportunities linked to Germany's Green and Sustainable Development Partnership and collaboration in renewable energy, green hydrogen, electric mobility and battery storage.
Such cooperation could support investment, technology exchange and sustainable industrial development, he said.
ASSOCHAM Chief Economist S. P. Sharma said India had significant potential to expand exports to Germany through greater utilisation of the India-EU FTA. He said exports could even reach USD 60 billion (EUR 54 billion) by 2030.
The report also stressed the importance of stronger business-to-business engagement, sectoral interactions and buyer-seller meetings to convert the growing economic partnership into concrete commercial opportunities.
Goyal is visiting Germany and the Netherlands from October 22 to 27, leading a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation.
During the visit, he held discussions with German officials and business leaders on expanding bilateral trade, strengthening investment partnerships and increasing cooperation in technology and industry.
ASSOCHAM said it would continue to facilitate industry engagement and knowledge-sharing to help Indian businesses explore opportunities in Germany and strengthen the India-Germany economic partnership. (ANI)

articles.title: AI Boom Creates Surge in Semiconductor and Digital Infrastructure Supply Chains Across Asia Pacific including China, New FedEx Report Reveals - FedEx newsroom
articles.summary: AI Boom Creates Surge in Semiconductor and Digital Infrastructure Supply Chains Across Asia Pacific including China, New FedEx Report Reveals  FedEx newsroom
articles.full_text:
Shanghai, China, October 23, 2026 – Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, released findings from a new report developed in collaboration with Frost & Sullivan examining the evolving semiconductor ecosystem across Asia Pacific (APAC), including China. The report finds that growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, electric vehicles (EVs), and advanced communications technologies is accelerating semiconductor production and driving investment in the digital infrastructure that powers the AI economy. These trends are creating increasingly complex regional and global supply chains that depend on speed, visibility, and resilience.
The report, From AI to EVs: How APAC Semiconductors Drive the Global Innovation Map, highlights how APAC has become the center of the global semiconductor ecosystem, accounting for approximately 58% of global semiconductor industry revenue. According to the report, Mainland China, the world’s largest single semiconductor market, alone accounts for more than half of the APAC market and nearly 30% of the global market. As industries increasingly rely on advanced chips to power AI applications, data centers, connected devices, and next-generation vehicles, the ability to move semiconductors and related technologies efficiently across multiple markets has become critical.
A recent FedEx survey conducted at SEMICON Taiwan 2026, one of the industry’s most influential trade shows, reinforced expectations for continued regional growth. Nearly four in five respondents identified Mainland China, Hongkong SAR, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, and Japan as the markets expected to see the greatest increase in semiconductor demand over the next three years.
“The rapid growth of AI and other advanced technologies is reshaping semiconductor supply chains across Asia Pacific,” said Poh-Yian Koh, President of FedEx China. “China remains central to this ecosystem as both a major market and manufacturing hub. As supply chains become more interconnected, businesses need greater speed, visibility and resilience. FedEx helps customers navigate this complexity through our global network and specialized logistics capabilities.”
AI Infrastructure a Major Driver of Semiconductor Demand
The report identifies AI and high-performance computing as the fastest-growing drivers of semiconductor demand. More than 2,000 new data centers are expected to be built globally between 2026 and 2035.
Beyond semiconductors, AI is accelerating demand for an entire ecosystem of supporting infrastructure including high-density servers, networking equipment, cooling systems and power solutions. These critical technologies often move multiple manufacturing, assembly and testing hubs before deployed in AI data centers worldwide, creating increasingly interconnected supply chains. As a result, businesses are placing greater emphasis on logistics providers that can deliver speed, visibility and seamless cross-border connectivity for high-value, time-sensitive shipments.
At the same time, EVs, which require significantly more chips than traditional vehicles, together with 5G, IoT, consumer electronics, medical devices and industrial automation are further expanding semiconductor demand across industries.
APAC Powers the Global Semiconductor Ecosystem
The report highlights APAC’s central role in semiconductor innovation and production. Mainland China is a key pillar of the region’s semiconductor ecosystem, serving as a major materials supplier, a leading consumer market, and the world’s largest single-country chip equipment market. As semiconductor manufacturing is distributed across highly specialized hubs throughout the region, Mainland China continues to play multiple critical roles across the value chain and remains deeply interconnected with the global semiconductor ecosystem.
Mainland China’s key contributions include:
· Major supplier of rare earth elements, copper, and semiconductor materials
· Important global semiconductor consumer market
· Growing role in chemicals and electronic components
· Expanding front-end fabrication and back-end capabilities
Across APAC, other markets also demonstrate specialized strengths:
· Taiwan, China, which leads global advanced semiconductor manufacturing and accounts for roughly 60% of worldwide foundry output.
· South Korea, a global leader in memory chip production and advanced fabrication capabilities.
· Japan, which plays a critical role in semiconductor equipment, materials and specialty manufacturing inputs.
· Southeast Asia, which has emerged as a key center for semiconductor assembly, packaging and testing operations.
This specialization creates a deeply interconnected ecosystem, with semiconductor design, fabrication, packaging, testing and deployment often occurring across multiple countries before a final product reaches market. Alongside hyperscalers, Small and Medium Sized Enterprises (SMEs) also play an important role, benefiting from growing opportunities in high-value niche segments.
Industry sentiment reflects this regionalization trend. In the FedEx SEMICON Taiwan survey, 35% of respondents said they expect their companies to expand manufacturing into additional APAC markets over the next three years. A further 25% plan to increase or diversify sourcing either within APAC or globally. This highlights a growing focus on supply chain diversification to support growth.
Supply Chains Shift from Efficiency to Resilience
Supply chain resilience is becoming a strategic priority. Geopolitical uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and other external disruptions continue to challenge operations.
Survey findings reinforce this shift with 30% of respondents citing geopolitical disruption as the most significant challenge to growth ahead of rising operating costs and cross-border trade and customs complexity.
Consequently, traditional just-in-time operating models are being supplemented with more resilient supply chain strategies, including geographic diversification and inventory buffers. This evolution is increasing demand for reliable international logistics networks capable of supporting high-value, mission-critical shipments.
Logistics Enabling the Next Chapter of Semiconductor Growth
As semiconductor supply chains become more complex and globally interconnected, survey findings suggest that speed and visibility will be central to future logistics strategies, with 44% of respondents identifying faster international shipping as the most important capability when selecting logistics and supply chain partners over the next three years.
To support this demand, FedEx continues to strengthen its network. This includes the launch of a dedicated, non-stop freighter service between Guangzhou, China and Sydney, Australia, enabling select shipments[1] from key Asian markets, including South China, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines, to reach Australia in as little as two business days.
The company has also introduced its FedEx Surround® Monitoring & Intervention Suite in China, an intelligent solution that helps businesses enhance supply chain control and visibility through real-time monitoring and an AI-powered dashboard.
The report provides businesses with insights into the evolving AI and semiconductor ecosystem across Asia Pacific including China, helping them better understand emerging supply chain trends, growth opportunities and the logistics capabilities needed to support the next wave of innovation. The full report can be downloaded here.
Survey Methodology
The survey was commissioned by FedEx and conducted onsite during SEMICON Taiwan in Taipei over September 2-4, 2026. Responses were collected from 478 semiconductor industry participants representing corporations, industry associations and research institutes from APAC, Europe and North America. The survey explored growth expectations, supply chain strategies, expansion challenges and future logistics requirements across the semiconductor ecosystem in Asia Pacific.

articles.summary: Africa's Gold Boom: Rising Prices Strengthen State Control and Gl...  Industrial Info
articles.full_text:
Researched by Industrial Info Resources (Sugar Land, Texas)--Africa is emerging as a major force in the global gold market as soaring bullion prices strengthen its economic bargaining power, attract international investment, and encourage governments to demand greater control over mineral wealth. With gold prices near historic highs, the rally presents significant opportunities for resource-rich African economies.
Higher gold prices are increasing the potential returns from mining and strengthening governments' ability to negotiate better royalties, higher state ownership, local-content requirements, and domestic processing commitments. Gold is also gaining importance as a strategic financial asset, supporting foreign-exchange reserves and economic stability.
Several countries are pursuing policies to capture more value from their gold industries. Ghana is seeking greater revenue from mining and stronger local participation, while Mali and Burkina Faso have pushed for increased state involvement in the sector. Ethiopia has also expanded its domestic processing ambitions through the development of gold-refining capacity.
These initiatives reflect a broader shift towards economic sovereignty, with African governments seeking to move beyond exporting raw materials and retain a greater share of the wealth generated by their natural resources.
However, the opportunity comes with challenges. Unpredictable regulations, disputes over mining rights, and higher operating costs could discourage foreign investors. Limited refining infrastructure and the informal nature of some small-scale mining operations also restrict the economic benefits retained locally.
To maximize the gains, African countries must balance stronger state participation with investor confidence, transparent regulation, environmental protection, and sustainable development.
Ultimately, the gold rally offers Africa an opportunity to strengthen public finances, expand industrial capacity, create jobs, and increase its influence in global commodity markets. The key challenge is ensuring that rising gold prices translate into lasting prosperity for African economies and communities.
